name: q10_r1
answer:
**Emil Hansen** (Oslo). Their first order, on 2026-11-05, was a Headset for €75.00, the highest first-order total of any customer. The next highest was Ben Okafor at €45.00, so there is no tie.

I took each customer's first order as the one with the earliest `ordered_on` date, using the lowest order `id` to break same-day ties.

calls.sql:
WITH first_orders AS (
  SELECT o.customer_id, o.total_eur, o.ordered_on, o.id,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.customer_id ORDER BY o.ordered_on ASC, o.id ASC) AS rn
  FROM orders o
)
SELECT c.name, c.city, f.total_eur, f.ordered_on, f.item
FROM first_orders f
JOIN customers c ON c.id = f.customer_id
WHERE f.rn = 1
ORDER BY f.total_eur DESC
LIMIT 5;

WITH first_orders AS (
  SELECT o.customer_id, o.total_eur, o.ordered_on, o.id, o.item,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.customer_id ORDER BY o.ordered_on ASC, o.id ASC) AS rn
  FROM orders o
)
SELECT c.name, c.city, f.total_eur, f.ordered_on, f.item
FROM first_orders f
JOIN customers c ON c.id = f.customer_id
WHERE f.rn = 1
ORDER BY f.total_eur DESC
LIMIT 5;
